text:
maya: quick sanity check — brought up a new Liminal embed model (fp16 -> int8 per-channel). Running our normal recall@k suite and seeing a surprising drop at R@1 on short queries. tagging @sam @oliver for triage

sam: upload the eval run? which dataset/holdout?

maya: small repro run on wiki-short-1000 holdout, script: `./eval_embeddings --model liminal-v2-int8 --batch 16 --holdout wiki-short-1000`

ci-bot: results uploaded: https://ci.redwood/liminal/evals/6234567890 (artifacts: embeddings.npy, recall_report.json, kmeans_out.png) :white_check_mark:

sam: quick peek — recall@1 dropped from 0.82 -> 0.74, recall@5 0.95 -> 0.94. so top-1 mostly affected. any sign of centroid flipping?

oliver: can you paste recall_report.json snippet? curious about avg similarity for positive pairs vs nearest neighbor distances. also what indexing (cosine vs dot)?

maya: cosine. paste: 
```
R@1: 0.74
R@5: 0.94
mean_pos_similarity: 0.78
mean_nn_similarity: 0.80
```
(weird that mean_nn_similarity > mean_pos_similarity)

deepti: that suggests embedding space shifted so negatives are closer — could be quantization bias on certain dims. did you use per-channel scale?

maya: yes per-channel symmetric quant, runtime uses 6-bit-ish layout internally but export was int8. I can re-export with asymmetric zero-point and re-run.

sam: before that, run a quick kmeans silhouette to see cluster collapse: `python -c "from sklearn.metrics import silhouette_score; print(silhouette_score(X, labels, metric='cosine'))"`

oliver: I pulled kmeans_out.png from CI — attaching inline: small clusters have high overlap, silhouette ~0.12 (was 0.31 on fp16).

maya: confirmed: silhouette 0.12, cluster counts skewed (one huge cluster ~45% of points).

sam: do we have per-dim quant error stats? l2 per-dim before/after quant?

maya: yes small table in artifacts: top 5 dims with largest delta: dims [12, 87, 190, 3, 256] — relative error up to 0.42.

oliver: ok that smells like bias on certain dims dominating cosine metric for short queries. try re-scaling those dims post-quant (per-dim calibration) and re-eval. also try running with L2-normalization after quant (we usually normalize before indexing, but check order).

maya: doing two quick runs: (1) asymmetric int8 export, (2) per-dim calibration + re-normalize after quant. kicking off now, will paste numbers.

ci-bot: job 6234567891 started (run: asym-int8)
ci-bot: job 6234567892 started (run: per-dim-calib)

sam: also try shorter batch (batch16 -> batch4) — we saw batching artifacts once where micro-batching affected kernel clamping behavior on GPU. small chance but cheap to check.

maya: noted, will add batch4 run as job 6234567893.

ci-bot: job 6234567891 finished: R@1 0.76, R@5 0.945, silhouette 0.18

ci-bot: job 6234567892 finished: R@1 0.81, R@5 0.95, silhouette 0.29 

maya: per-dim calibration fixed most of it — R@1 nearly back to baseline. looks like quantization zero-point choice + per-channel scale mismatch between training stat and export.

oliver: nice. can you capture the calibration transform and add to model export pipeline? we should also add a quick unit-test: sample 1k holdout, ensure mean_nn_similarity <= mean_pos_similarity by margin.

deepti: agree. also add a regression alert in Optimize: if silhouette drops > 0.1 vs baseline, flag.

maya: opened PR: https://git.redwood/inference/liminal/patches/42 — adds asymmetric export + per-dim calibrator and a post-quant normalization. deployable as opt-in until we verify no perf regression.

sam: can we run a perf/p99 latency check for the per-dim step on CPU/GPU? might add tiny overhead at load time.

maya: quick numbers: per-dim calibrate on model load adds ~12ms cold-start, no impact to per-request runtime. I'll add note in PR.

oliver: cool. next steps: (1) merge PR behind feature flag, (2) run full holdout sweep (wiki, short-qa, stack-exchange), (3) run recall/regression job in nightly. good triage. :tada:

maya: thanks all. closing for now, will ping when full sweep done. :wave:
